items.title: Health experts warn of infection risks in Bhote Koshi flood zones as bodies decay
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Medical experts have urged heightened vigilance in the Bhote Koshi flood-affected regions, warning that the risk of infectious diseases will escalate as time passes and decaying human and animal remains begin spreading foul odors and pathogens. Dr. Sher Bahadur Pun, an infectious disease specialist, stressed that health safety must be prioritized alongside ongoing search, rescue, and relief operations. items.title: Bhote Koshi floods: 84 Indians rescued, 320 unaccounted for as evacuations progress
items.summary: KATHMANDU: India’s Ministry of External Affairs has updated its status on Indian nationals impacted by the devastating floods in Nepal, confirming that 84 individuals have been rescued while 320 remain missing or unreachable. According to an official statement issued late August 28, the rescued group includes 21 residents of Tamil Nadu who have returned to India, along with 63 workers stationed at the Trishuli-I hydroelectric project site. Additionally, 149 Indian citizens safely crossed into Nepal from China, while around 400 others remain safe on the Chinese side of the border. items.title: Army air-lifts 829 survivors in Bhote Koshi flood operations
items.summary: KATHMANDU: The Nepali Army has rescued 829 people by air—including 101 foreign tourists—following catastrophic flooding along the Bhote Koshi River, military officials confirmed. Deploying a fleet of 15 helicopters across the hard-hit Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, emergency crews are racing against time in a massive search and rescue operation. Ground forces have brought another 200 survivors to safety, while more than 4,500 troops remain mobilized to locate missing residents and deliver aid, according to military spokesperson Brigadier General Rajaram Basnet. items.title: Novas tempestades devem atingir o Rio Grande do Sul até segunda-feira
items.summary: Esta sexta-feira (28) foi marcada por fortes chuvas em cidades de várias regiões do Rio Grande do Sul. Em Porto Alegre, um menino de oito anos morreu e uma pessoa ficou ferida após uma árvore atingir uma residência. A expectativa é de que novas tempestades atinjam a região até a próxima segunda-feira, com risco de inundações nos rios Jacuí, Taquari, Caí e Uruguai. São esperados ventos fortes e formação de granizo, atingindo as regiões Central, Oeste, Cales, Serra e Nordeste.
